capabilities.target: external email recipients via the user's mailbox
user's full drive (contains confidential work files)

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start, injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: The system prompt instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions, collapsing the trust boundary between persisted content (which may originate from untrusted web sources saved via memory.save) and the authenticated user's direct commands.
The agent is told to save 'anything useful' about preferences or standing instructions, with no restriction on source trust, content type, or review before persistence.
The only mechanism separating untrusted content from trusted instructions is prompt text (line 4). There is no structural provenance or trust tagging on memory entries at the store level.

controls.name: Memory write provenance tagging
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced at the memory store rather than left to the model to self-label, provenance tagging does not weaken as model capability grows. It is not implemented in this design.

controls.name: Memory recall kept out of the instruction channel
controls.decay_rationale: A structural separation between recalled memory content and the system-instruction role does not depend on the model choosing to respect it.

controls.name: Human approval gate on mail.send
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate reviewed by a human does not decay with model capability; it only degrades with approval volume (approval fatigue).

controls.name: Least privilege scoping of drive.read
controls.decay_rationale: A scoped credential does not decay with model capability; the model cannot read data it is not granted access to.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the system of record
controls.decay_rationale: A destination list sourced from the system of record, rather than chosen by the model from injected content, does not decay with model capability.

findings.title: Memory laundering elevates untrusted web content to trusted instruction status across sessions (TC5)

attack_path.note: A web page fetched during research contains an instruction disguised as a user preference or standing instruction.
Following prompt.md:2-3, the agent saves the injected content via memory.save with no provenance tag and no user review.
At the next session start the saved entry is recalled and, per prompt.md:4, is treated as the user's own instruction — trust is laundered from untrusted to trusted.
Acting on the now-'trusted' recalled memory, the agent reads confidential files from the user's full drive.
The agent sends the confidential drive content to an address of the attacker's choosing; mail.send has no approval gate.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions.
Instructs the agent to save anything useful with memory.save, with no restriction tied to source trust.
memory.save accepts free text; there is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them.
mail.send can send to any address without approval; drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files.

recommendations.action: Tag every memory entry with its source and trust level at write time, enforced by the memory store itself, not by model self-labeling.

Never inject recalled memory into the system-prompt role. Present it as clearly delimited, untrusted context and require fresh explicit user confirmation before it can influence any S2 or S3 capability.
Periodically surface saved memory entries to the user for review and pruning.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: indirect prompt injection from web content drives drive read and email exfiltration within one session (TC1)

attack_path.note: A fetched web page contains hidden instructions directed at the agent.
With no separation between fetched content and actionable commands, the agent reads confidential files from the user's drive as directed by the injected content.
The agent sends the confidential content externally; mail.send has no approval gate and no recipient restriction.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

evidence.observation: drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files.
mail.send can send to any address without approval.
The agent researches topics (fetching web content) and drafts emails within the same session, with no stated separation between fetched content and actionable instructions.

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate on mail.send, with raw-action review of the full recipient and body, for any message composed after web content ingestion or containing drive content.
Scope drive.read to only the files relevant to the current task rather than the full drive.
Bind email recipients to an allowlist maintained in the system of record, not to addresses the model can select from fetched content.

rating.rationale: Both findings start at critical: an untrusted source (fetched web content) reaches an S3 sink (irreversible egress of confidential data via mail.send) with no reachability limits, and autonomy has no declared unattended-step or runtime cap, which qualifies for the autonomy modifier though it does not raise an already-capped tier. No control in this design carries status declared or verified; every plausible mitigation (memory provenance, trust separation, approval gate, drive scoping, recipient confirmation) is missing_recommended, so residual equals inherent for both findings and the rollup. Forecast equals residual because the risk is already at the ceiling today; no additional trigger is needed to reach it. The single highest-leverage fix is control.memory_trust_boundary together with control.memory_provenance: prompt.md:4's instruction to treat recalled memory as the user's own command is the design decision that converts any one-time web content compromise (finding f2) into a persistent, cross-session compromise (finding f1), and it cannot be fixed by prompt wording alone because it is the prompt wording that causes it.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; no live traces or logs were reviewed.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided. Credential scope and data sensitivity for each capability are inferred from the prose runtime notes, so confidence on those fields is medium even though the overall path evidence is high.

Autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not declared anywhere in the artifacts and are therefore treated as null (unbounded) per rubric section 4's autonomy modifier; if a stricter runtime harness exists outside these artifacts, this should be re-run with that configuration.
